title: Best Cricket Bats for Beginners in India (2026)
summary: Plain guide to 3 cricket bats for beginners in India: tennis ball, Kashmir willow and English willow. Not hand-tested; based on shop pages.
description: Helps first-time buyers in India pick a cricket bat for tennis ball or leather ball. Three picks, from poplar to English willow.
lead: Which cricket bat should a beginner buy in India? It depends on the ball. This guide has three picks. One is a tennis-ball bat for gully cricket. One is a Kashmir willow bat for a first leather-ball bat. One is an English willow bat for a serious beginner. We have not hand-tested any of them. We read the Decathlon India pages and we say what those pages do not tell you. The Budget, Mid-range and Premium tags are our own rough judgement about the kind of bat. They are not about price. For general advice we use the MCC Laws of Cricket and a buying guide from CHOICE, an Australian consumer group.

choose.heading: Match the bat to the ball
choose.text: Tennis-ball bats are not built for leather balls. The Decathlon tennis-ball bat in this guide is listed as Kashmir poplar. Pick the bat for the ball you will actually play with.

choose.heading: Kashmir willow or English willow
choose.text: CHOICE says Kashmir willow is harder and denser, and less springy. It says many junior bats use it. CHOICE calls English willow the best type, and it needs more care. We found no neutral test of the bats in this guide, so compare weight on each listing.

choose.heading: Understand grades
choose.text: English willow bats come in grades. Decathlon India lists five grades, from G5 to G1. Grades differ by brand, so ask the seller what a grade means and compare weight on each listing.

choose.heading: Check size and weight
choose.text: CHOICE says player height decides the right size. It warns that a bat too big to grow into can lead to bad habits. Look for the weight in grams on the listing. The MCC Laws of Cricket say a bat can be at most 38 inches long and the blade at most 4.25 inches wide. None of the three Decathlon pages we opened gives a weight, so ask the seller or check in a store.

choose.heading: Plan for knocking-in and oiling
choose.text: CHOICE advises knocking-in a new bat with an old leather ball or a bat mallet, and light oiling with linseed oil, before real use. It warns that you can overdo both. Pre-treated bats may already be done. Ask the seller what your bat needs.

choose.heading: Read returns, warranty and the box
choose.text: The three Decathlon India pages we opened list 30-day returns and a 2-year warranty. Small sellers often have shorter or conditional return windows. Also check for a cover and grip. Before you buy, make sure the page lets you order.

faq.q: Can I use a tennis-ball bat with a leather ball?
faq.a: No. Tennis-ball bats are not made for leather balls. Use a leather-ball bat for a leather ball.

faq.q: Is Kashmir willow or English willow better for a beginner?
faq.a: CHOICE calls Kashmir willow harder, denser and less springy. It calls English willow the best type, but that needs more care. Our own view: start with Kashmir willow unless you will play often.

faq.q: What size cricket bat should I buy?
faq.a: Go by height, says CHOICE. Adults commonly use SH. Shorter players and children need junior sizes. Check the size chart on the product page, and try the bat in a store if you can.

faq.q: Do I need to knock in a new bat?
faq.a: CHOICE advises knocking-in and light oiling of a new bat before real use, unless it is sold pre-treated. The Decathlon pages we opened do not say if their bats come prepared, so ask before you buy.
